fact: At the first interministerial meeting on the national AI strategy, participants stressed the need to process, host and secure administrative data in national data centres, as part of a strategy with sovereign open-source government AI models and national computing capacity.

Algeria's sovereign National Digital Services Center, inaugurated days before 15 July 2026, has two Tier III-standard data centres in Algiers and Blida that will host government data, per authorities cited by We Are Tech.

The Prime Minister launched on 9 February 2026 the national data governance system under presidential decree of 30 December 2025, which he said aims to ensure control, organisation and protection of public data in a sovereign model.

High Commissioner Benmouloud said the strategic infrastructure is complete, with data centres in service, cloud accounts deployed and the sovereign IRIES network linking over 55 state bodies in a closed environment outside the Internet.

Ech-Chaab, citing the High Commission's record for April 2024 to September 2026, lists sovereign cloud computing, the secured government network and national data centres among delivered milestones, and the national digital services centre inaugurated on 5 July 2026.

We Are Tech (citing Agence Ecofin) reports the National Digital Services Center, two active-active data centers in Algiers and Blida inaugurated on 5 July 2026, now hosts all data generated by Algeria's public administrations on national territory.

El Watan reports President Tebboune inaugurated the Centre national algerien des services numeriques, built on two national data centres to host national data in Algeria, including the National Public Services Portal and the National Database.

The National Centre for Digital Services at Mohammadia, inaugurated 5 July 2026, is built on two national active-active data centres and runs the network, cloud computing platforms, the national public-services portal and the national database.

Le Jeune Indépendant says the centre, inaugurated 5 July 2026, serves administrations and companies as clients and is built to centralise state databases such as civil status, justice, tax and health.

fact: The Algerian government reviewed on 17 December 2025 the setting up of two strategic infrastructures forming Algeria's first national cloud, meant to secure and modernise public services by hosting sovereign data.

Algeria's High Commissioner for Digitalisation, Meriem Benmouloud, announced a planned national cloud, one for ministries and public bodies without data centres and one for the public and local firms, to host and secure national information systems, within the 2025-2030 national digital transformation strategy.
